advisories.message: The first two lessons retain explicit front-loaded polish and concrete wins. The 36-minute convolution opener should still be piloted to confirm that its three concepts and identification demo remain among the course's easiest experiences.

All 15 demo specifications pass D1 with a meaningful manipulation, target or numerical threshold, and falsification behavior. Responsiveness, accessible controls, useful presets, and implementation-size limits remain checks for the later component build.

Recorded audio and third-party visual evidence remain subject to the rights gates stated in the briefs and image registry; use the specified learner-owned, CC-licensed, or recomputed fallback when clearance is unavailable.

verification.non_extra_spiral: Every concept introduced on the non-extra path has at least three non-extra lesson encounters.
verification.prerequisite_ancestry: Every reinforced concept is reachable from its introduction through the lesson's prerequisite ancestors.
verification.optional_branch: Perfect-Reconstruction Filter Banks and Wavelet and Paraunitary Filter Banks remain extra; no core lesson depends on them, and all four multirate briefs quote the exact optional-branch caption.
verification.dither: Finite-Word Realizations now contains a definition, canonical case, boundary and near-miss cases, exact sources, seeded experiment, figure plan, and research-shaped exercise before later retrieval.
source_pointers: MIT 6.341 Lecture 7 pp. 1–20 and PS4 for structures and finite-word sensitivity
MIT 6.341 Lectures 10–11 and PS5–PS6 for multirate and polyphase processing
MIT 6.341 Lectures 21–22 and PS10 for STFT and modulated filter banks
Oppenheim–Schafer 2nd ed. Chapter 4 §§4.6–4.9, especially §4.6.1, for rate conversion and aliasing
MIT 6.341 Lecture 2 pp. 5–6 for generalized-linear-phase FIR symmetry
MIT 6.341 Lecture 9 pp. 4–6 for alternation and Parks–McClellan exchange
verification.brief_contracts: All 30 briefs match course slug/title/status/module/type/goal/time metadata and contain ARC, at least three exact sources, key points, pitfalls, source-grounded gems, figure plan, six or more exercises, and a complete application protocol for every synthesis lesson.
